title: Selberg sieve approach to primes minus factorials compositeness

problemStatement.formal: \operatorname{AFSC}(n) := \forall k,\ k! < n \Rightarrow \neg\operatorname{Prime}(n-k!) \wedge n-k! \ge 2.\quad \text{OQ-02 proves }(\forall l\ge 3,\exists p\in(l!,(l+1)!],\operatorname{Prime}(p)\wedge\operatorname{AFSC}(p))\Rightarrow \#\{p:\operatorname{Prime}(p)\wedge\operatorname{AFSC}(p)\}=\infty,\text{ with the displayed Selberg-density premise axiomatized.}
problemStatement.plain: Formalizes a Selberg-sieve route to Erdős Problem #1059. Primes are organized into factorial intervals I(l) = (l!, (l+1)!]; the Lean file proves the elementary interval and wrapper lemmas, then assumes a Selberg density axiom saying every sufficiently high level contains a qualifying prime.
whyMatters: It isolates the analytic number theory still missing from Mathlib: prime-counting estimates, Brun-Titchmarsh, and a Selberg upper-bound sieve for the shifted-prime obstruction.
The proved Lean wrapper shows that a per-interval qualifying-prime existence statement is enough to imply infinitely many primes p for which every p - k! below p is composite.
The companion correction file gives concrete evidence that the original l >= 3 threshold is too strong: all primes in I(3) = (6, 24] fail, while p = 101 qualifies in I(4).

proven: In Erdos1059OQ02.lean, AllFactorialSubtractionsComposite and ErdosProblem1059 are defined for the factorial-subtraction property and infinitude target.
PrimorialInterval(l) = Finset.Ioc(l!, (l+1)!) is defined, with |I(l)| = l * l! proved and nonemptiness proved for l >= 1.
factorial_bound_in_interval proves that if p lies in I(l) and k! < p, then k <= l.
prime_in_primorial_interval proves an equivalence between AFSC(p) and checking only the factorial indices up to the interval level l.
BadFactorialIndices and condition_count_at_level formalize the finite set of shifted-prime obstructions and prove it has size at most l + 1.
primorial_intervals_disjoint proves different factorial intervals are disjoint.
selberg_implies_erdos proves the wrapper implication from the axiomatized Selberg density statement to Erdős Problem #1059.
In Erdos1059OQ02OQ01.lean, six norm_num-backed lemmas prove that 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, and 23 each fail AFSC, covering the primes in I(3).
Erdos1059OQ02OQ01.lean proves p101_prime and p101_qualifying, verifying that 101 is a qualifying prime in I(4).
Both OQ-02 and OQ-02-OQ-01 have 0 sorries in their local metadata.
open: selberg_density_axiom in Erdos1059OQ02.lean is axiomatized and depends on analytic tools not yet supplied by Mathlib.
The l >= 3 form of selberg_density_axiom is locally shown to have a threshold bug: the companion file proves no prime in I(3) qualifies.
selberg_density_corrected in Erdos1059OQ02OQ01.lean replaces the threshold by l >= 4 but is still an axiom for the general case.
A proof of the corrected density axiom would require formal Brun-Titchmarsh/Selberg-sieve estimates for the shifted-prime sets.
knownResults.goal: Replace the axiomatized Selberg density premise with a real Lean proof, using the corrected l >= 4 threshold established by the companion analysis.

knowledge.progressSummary: OQ-02 contains a complete Lean wrapper around one analytic axiom: interval structure, obstruction counting, disjointness, and the implication from a per-level Selberg density premise to Erdős #1059 are proved with 0 sorries. The sibling correction file proves the original l >= 3 threshold is false at l = 3 and supplies the conservative corrected axiom l >= 4.
builtItems: AllFactorialSubtractionsComposite: predicate requiring every p - k! with k! < p to be non-prime and at least 2.
PrimorialInterval(l): factorial interval (l!, (l+1)!] implemented as Finset.Ioc.
primorial_interval_size: Lean proof that |I(l)| = l * l!.
factorial_bound_in_interval: Lean proof that only k <= l need be checked for p in I(l).
prime_in_primorial_interval: Lean equivalence between global AFSC and finite interval-level checks.
BadFactorialIndices and condition_count_at_level: finite obstruction set and cardinality bound.
primorial_intervals_disjoint: Lean proof that different factorial intervals do not overlap.
selberg_implies_erdos: Lean theorem deriving ErdosProblem1059 from selberg_density_axiom.
p7_fails, p11_fails, p13_fails, p17_fails, p19_fails, p23_fails: companion Lean proofs that all primes in I(3) fail AFSC.
p101_qualifying: companion Lean proof that 101 satisfies AFSC in I(4).
infinitely_many_qualifying_primes: companion Lean theorem using selberg_density_corrected to get arbitrarily large qualifying primes.
insights: The formalized elementary layer is real Lean proof; the existence of qualifying primes in every high factorial interval is not proved and remains an axiom.
The original OQ-02 axiom is stronger than the evidence supports: l = 3 is a concrete counterexample to the stated threshold.
The corrected threshold l >= 4 is sharp at the base level because 101 is verified as a qualifying prime in I(4).

The wrapper theorem does not depend on disjointness directly for its Lean proof: it obtains arbitrarily large qualifying primes by choosing l = n + 3 in the original file, while the corrected file chooses l = n + 4.
A future analytic proof should count primes p in I(l) for which some shifted value p - k! is prime, then show at least one prime avoids all such shifts.
mathlibGaps: Brun-Titchmarsh inequality for shifted prime counts in factorial intervals.
Selberg upper-bound sieve or comparable sieve estimates for the bad factorial-index union.
Prime-counting estimates strong enough to compare good and bad prime counts in I(l).
nextSteps: Update any future formal route to use the corrected l >= 4 threshold rather than the parent file's l >= 3 axiom.
Formalize the analytic inequality behind selberg_density_corrected, separating finite base cases from the asymptotic sieve argument.
Compare the Selberg-density axiom with the smooth-number axiom in Erdos1059Problem.lean and the density-one route in OQ-04.

papers: Selberg, A. "On an elementary method in the theory of primes" (1947), cited in Proofs/Erdos1059OQ02.lean.
Selberg, A. "On the normal density of primes in small intervals" (1943), cited in src/data/proofs/erdos-1059-oq-02-oq-01/meta.json.
